page.name: Normalized delivery receipts
page.metaTitle: Delivery receipts — one status, every provider
page.metaDescription: Providers report delivery in their own vocabulary. The platform normalizes those receipts into one status your systems can read.
page.lede: Two providers describe the same outcome with two different words, and neither word means what the reader assumes. Normalizing receipts into one status is what makes a receipt usable in code rather than as a screenshot.

p: Receipt collection and normalization run on every channel whose provider reports delivery back: on SMS that is every provider we connect, on email it is Resend, and on WhatsApp it is Meta. Whichever account carried the message, your system reads one normalized status — delivered, failed, or still awaiting a receipt — instead of a provider-specific word it has to translate itself. That is what makes a receipt usable in code.

sections.h: What a receipt actually tells you
p: A delivery receipt says the destination network accepted the message. It does not say a human read it, and it does not say the handset displayed it. Treating a receipt as proof of reading is the most common misreading of the data.
bullets: Accepted by the destination network — the normal reading of a delivery receipt
Rejected with a reason — carries the provider’s error, normalized where possible
No receipt at all — the message may still have arrived; absence is not proof of failure

p: Receipts are recorded against the message log and can be pushed to an endpoint you configure, so a system that needs to react does not have to poll. Callback delivery has its own reliability characteristics, which the guides cover explicitly rather than glossing over.

faq.q: Do receipts work for email and WhatsApp?
faq.a: Where the provider reports delivery back, yes. Every SMS provider we connect does; on email that is Resend, and on WhatsApp that is Meta. The other providers in each channel are connected for sending today, and their delivery events are not wired back yet — the provider pages on /integrations/ say which is which.

faq.q: Can I tell whether a message was read?
faq.a: No. A receipt reflects acceptance by the destination network, not attention from the recipient.

faq.q: What if a receipt never arrives?
faq.a: Absence of a receipt is not the same as failure. The messages-not-arriving help article walks through how to tell the two apart.
